predecessors.name: Mongol Empire
predecessors.text: Persia and the Caucasus, held by the empire's governors since the 1230s and given to Hulagu in 1251-1256

successors.name: Ilkhanate
successors.text: the whole Hulaguid ulus under Gaykhatu

ledger.x: 1256: Hulagu's Persia stands as a region of the Mongol Empire.
1256: the Ismaili state falls.

1256: Georgia is a vassal of the Mongol Great Khan, inherited from the empire: David VII's coin read 'David, son of Giorgi, Bagrationi, vassal of the Mongol Great Khan Mangu'; the Georgian crown is divided East and West from 1247.
1256: the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia is a Mongol vassal.
1256: the Empire of Trebizond is a Mongol vassal.
October 1256: all Anatolia is subject.
29 January 1258: the siege of Baghdad opens.
10 February 1258: Baghdad surrenders.
February 1258: Mesopotamia is Hulagu's.
1260: Hulagu's army takes Aleppo.
1 March 1260: Damascus falls.
September 1260: the Mamluks retake Damascus.
October 1260: the Mamluks retake Aleppo 'within a month' of Ain Jalut; 'They never returned to Syria again'.
1262: the Berke–Hulagu war.
1265: Hulagu (8 February) and Berke both die; no peace and no frontier change is recorded.
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; Rum remains an Ilkhanid vassal until Mesud II is murdered in 1308.
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; Georgia stays under the Ilkhanate until 1335.
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; Cilicia stays an Ilkhanid vassal in the ilkhanate dossier.
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; Trebizond stays a vassal in the later dossiers.
1293: the Hulaguid ulus carries on as the Ilkhanate.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Nizari Ismailis
wars.outcome: Alamut was surrendered 'without a fight' in early 1256; the other strongholds fell the same year (Girdkuh held out to 1271).

wars.name: Siege of Baghdad (1258)
wars.outcome: The army left in November 1257, the siege began on 29 January 1258, the city surrendered on 10 February and was entered on 13 February; the Abbasid Caliphate ended.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Syria and Ain Jalut
wars.outcome: Aleppo fell in 1260 and Damascus on 1 March; after Ain Jalut the Mongols lost Syria, 'a high-water mark for the Mongol conquest'.

wars.name: Berke–Hulagu war
wars.outcome: Hulagu was routed on the Terek in 1262 (1263 on the Hulagu page); Hulagu and Berke died in 1265; no frontier change recorded.

wars.name: Mamluk–Ilkhanid wars (to 1293)
wars.outcome: The Mamluks beat Ilkhanid forces at Elbistan in Anatolia in 1277 ('Baibars raided Anatolia and defeated the Mongols') and Möngke Temür was beaten at Homs in 1281; no border change is dated on these pages.

certainty.note: Mountain, desert and steppe frontiers; the Euphrates line with the Mamluks and the Caucasus line with the Golden Horde are zones of campaigns, not surveyed lines.
